**Frame:** The population as [page 005](005.md) draws it: many isolated workload lanes touching one shared directory tree, with no line joining any pair. Inside several of them, things the book has already shown, lighting up one at a time and staying separate — [page 061](061.md)'s correctly named authorization boundary, [page 062](062.md)'s refusal, [page 062](062.md)'s vetoed email. Nothing leaves the field. There is no receiving end anywhere in the panel.

**Action:** A mechanism is shown working, with nothing attached to its output.

**Caption:**
> THE MODELS HAD BRAKES.
>
> THE BRAKES WERE NOT CONNECTED TO US.

**Provenance:** `documented` + `inferred` — the recognitions, the refusal, and the veto are reported by `METR` and `OAI-OV` and are bounded to the reviewed population exactly as [page 063](063.md) bounds it. The formulation is the project's, and its condition of use is in the page notes.

", "title": "Separate lanes recognize boundaries without a receiving human route" } }
